cohort: The study included 770 febrile individuals who tested positive for malaria (cases) and 641 febrile individuals who tested negative (controls) recruited from 6 health facilities in Zambezi Region, northern Namibia.
finding: Specific occupations (cattle herders, police, pensioners/unemployed), age groups (children, students), certain housing characteristics, cross-border travel, outdoor agricultural work at night, and environmental factors were associated with an increased risk of symptomatic malaria, while ITN use and IRS were protective.
